title: Refining a pointed devissage along elementary etale target and base maps
statement: Let $(Z,Y,i,\pi,\mathcal G,z,y,d)$ be a pointed affine one-step datum for $(\mathcal F,X,B,x,b)$ as defined in [def-trf-pointed-scheme-devissage-data]. Suppose there is a commutative square of pointed schemes $(Y',y')\to(Y,y)$ over $(B',b')\to(B,b)$ whose horizontal maps are elementary etale. Then there exist an affine elementary etale map $(B'',b'')\to(B',b')$, an affine open $Y''\subset Y'\times_{B'}B''$ containing its distinguished point $y''$, and an elementary etale map $(X'',x'')\to(X,x)$ over $B''\to B$, with $Z''=Z\times_YY''$, such that the pulled-back finite morphism $\pi'':Z''\to Y''$, a closed immersion $i'':Z''\hookrightarrow X''$ of finite presentation, the pullbacks $\mathcal F'',\mathcal G''$, and the marked points form a pointed affine one-step datum of the same smooth relative dimension $d$. The square with sides $i'',i,X''\to X,Z''\to Z$ is cartesian. With $h:Y''\to Y$, there is a canonical isomorphism $h^*(\pi_*\mathcal G)\cong\pi''_*\mathcal G''$. Consequently the pullback of any $\alpha:\mathcal O_Y^{\oplus r}\to\pi_*\mathcal G$ whose residue-field map at the generic point of $Y_b$ is an isomorphism has this same property at the generic point of $Y''_{b''}$, and its cokernel is $h^*\operatorname{coker}\alpha$. The map $h$ is elementary at the marked points; in particular $\kappa(y'')=\kappa(y)$ and $\kappa(b'')=\kappa(b)$ via the induced maps. All terminology, tensor pullbacks, fibre products, and cokernels are as in [def-trf-pointed-scheme-devissage-data].

source.place: Tag 05HE (lemma-elementary-etale-neighbourhood), diagram and proof; the same construction for the auxiliary datum omitting support-dimension equalities. Finite-pushforward base change and cokernels are the comparisons used in the proof of Tag 05HR (proposition-existence-complete-at-x).

proof.text: Choose an affine open $A\subset B'$ containing $b'$, then an affine open $U\subset Y'\times_{B'}A$ containing $y'$, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. The composite $U\to Y$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], and elementary at $y'$ because open immersions preserve residue fields [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality]. The map $U\to Y\times_B A$ is etale: its composite to $Y$ and the projection to $Y$ are etale, the latter by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], so apply cancellation. First, $Y\to B$ is smooth of relative dimension $d$ in the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]: it is locally of finite presentation between affine schemes, hence of finite presentation and so of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so each fibre $Y_t$ is of finite type over $\kappa(t)$ by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]; it is irreducible of dimension $d$ by [def-trf-pointed-scheme-devissage-data], so $\dim_{y_1}Y_t=\dim Y_t=d$ at every $y_1\in Y_t$ by [lem-sc-dimension-locally-algebraic]. Hence $U\to A$ is smooth of relative dimension $d$ by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence]. It is locally of finite presentation by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], since source and target are affine.

source.place: Tag 05HE (lemma-elementary-etale-neighbourhood), affine localization and smooth relative dimension in the proof.

proof.text: Put $k=\kappa(b')=\kappa(b)$. The marked residue field of $U$ is $\kappa(y')=\kappa(y)$, compatibly over $k$. This extension is purely transcendental by [def-trf-pointed-scheme-devissage-data]. Its transcendence basis is finite: $U_{b'}$ is of finite type over $k$ by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] (finite presentation implies finite type by the definitions), so [lem-kun-finite-type-residue-trdeg] gives finite transcendence degree; an algebraically independent generating set in [def-trf-purely-transcendental-extension] therefore has finite cardinality. Apply [lem-trf-finite-smooth-integral-base-refinement] to $S_0=A$, $Y_0=U$, $n=d$, and $W_0=U$ with $\pi_0=\mathrm{id}_U$ and $w_0=y_0=y'$. The identity is finite and its fibre is a singleton by definition. We obtain an affine elementary etale $(C,c)\to(A,b')$ and a quasi-compact open $V\subset U\times_A C$, smooth of relative dimension $d$ with geometrically integral fibres, containing a point $v$ with residue field $\kappa(y)$; also $\kappa(c)=\kappa(b)$.

source.place: Tag 05HE, final paragraph: select the component through the marked point and spread geometrically irreducible fibres; Tag 057K supplies the existing packaged component-spreading result.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $W\subset V$ containing $v$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. The morphism $V\to C$ is smooth, hence flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat], and open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. Thus its image of $W$ is an open neighbourhood of $c$. Choose a principal open $B''=D(a)\subset C$ containing $c$ and contained in this image by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open]. It is affine with open-immersion inclusion by [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion]. Put $Y''=W\times_C B''$. It is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], and open in $Y'\times_{B'}B''$. Every fibre is nonempty, by the choice of $D(a)$, and is an open subscheme of the corresponding geometrically integral fibre of $V$. After any field extension it remains nonempty by [lem-pc-field-extension-surjective] and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change], and open in an integral scheme, hence irreducible and reduced: any two nonempty opens intersect, and restrictions of a reduced structure sheaf are reduced. Thus these fibres are geometrically integral in [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Smooth relative dimension $d$ is unchanged by open restriction and base change, using [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] and the etaleness of open immersions. Each fibre $Y''_t$ is irreducible and of finite type over $\kappa(t)$ (an open of the finite-type affine $W_t$), and $\dim_{y_1}Y''_t=d$ at its points, so $\dim Y''_t=d$ by [lem-sc-dimension-locally-algebraic]. The marked point $y''$ is the restriction of $v$; the maps $(B'',b'')\to(B',b')$ and $h:(Y'',y'')\to(Y,y)$ are elementary by composition and open-immersion invariance of residue fields.

source.place: Tag 05HE, final two sentences: shrink first the target and then the base to make both affine without empty fibres.

proof.text: Set $Z''=Z\times_Y Y''$. The morphism $\pi'':Z''\to Y''$ is finite and $Z''$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence]. Its projection $e:Z''\to Z$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Every point over $y''$ maps to $z$, since $\pi^{-1}(y)=\{z\}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points], these points correspond to primes of $\kappa(z)\otimes_{\kappa(y)}\kappa(y'')$. The field map $\beta:\kappa(y)\to\kappa(y'')$ is an isomorphism, so $a\otimes b\mapsto a\,\pi^\sharp(\beta^{-1}(b))$ identifies this tensor ring with $\kappa(z)$. It has one prime. Denote the resulting point by $z''$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-point-residue-field], the canonical map $\kappa(z)\to\kappa(z'')$ is an isomorphism. This proves the singleton-fibre requirement and the pointed hypothesis for the ambient lift.

source.place: Tag 05HE, first paragraph and the finite/singleton-fibre verification in the second paragraph.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-pointed-etale-ambient-lift] with $S=B$, $S_1=B''$, $W=Z''$, $j=i$, $b=e$, and $r:Z''\to Y''\to B''$. Its base and $Z$ residue-field hypotheses were verified in steps 3 and 4. It supplies an affine $X''$, a closed immersion $i'':Z''\hookrightarrow X''$ of finite presentation, an elementary etale $(X'',x'')\to(X,x)$, and the required cartesian square, compatibly over $B''\to B$. Here $x''=i''(z'')$. In particular the source morphism to $B''$ is locally of finite type: $X\to B$ is finite type because it is locally finite type and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; $X\times_B B''$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], and its map to $B''$ is finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. The affine etale map $X''\to X\times_B B''$ is of finite presentation, hence finite type, by the same qcqs permanence statement. Composing gives finite type, hence locally finite type, over $B''$.

source.place: Tag 05HE, first paragraph: lift the affine etale neighbourhood across the closed immersion (Tag 057R); use B-double-prime consistently in the ambient base change.

proof.text: Let $g:X''\to X$, and put $\mathcal F''=g^*\mathcal F$, $\mathcal G''=e^*\mathcal G$. They are quasi-coherent and of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent] and [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-finite-type]. The closed immersion $i$ is affine: over an affine open of $X$ its inverse image is the spectrum of the quotient by its defining ideal [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Therefore the cartesian square in step 5 and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change](1) give $g^*i_*\mathcal G\cong i''_*e^*\mathcal G$. Pull back the specified isomorphism $i_*\mathcal G\cong\mathcal F$ to obtain $i''_*\mathcal G''\cong\mathcal F''$. Together with steps 3--5, this verifies every condition of [def-trf-pointed-scheme-devissage-data]: affineness, marked incidence, singleton finite fibre, smooth geometrically irreducible fibres of dimension $d$, finite-presentation closed immersion, and the module isomorphism. The field extension $\kappa(y'')/\kappa(b'')$ is the old purely transcendental extension through the induced field isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 05HE, second paragraph: affine base change of the closed pushforward; Tag 02KG (lemma-affine-base-change).

proof.text: The finite morphism $\pi$ is affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change](1) to its cartesian base change along $h$. The resulting canonical map is the required isomorphism $h^*(\pi_*\mathcal G)\cong\pi''_*\mathcal G''$. In particular it identifies the pulled-back $\alpha$ with a map $\alpha'':\mathcal O_{Y''}^{\oplus r}\to\pi''_*\mathcal G''$: [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf] identifies the structure sheaves, and finite direct sums in the tensor definition [def-pc-module-pullback] are carried to finite direct sums.

source.place: Tag 02KG (lemma-affine-base-change), applied to pi; the alpha comparison used in Tag 05HR.

proof.text: Write $\xi''$ and $\xi$ for the unique generic points of the nonempty irreducible fibres $Y''_{b''}$ and $Y_b$. The map $U\to Y\times_B A$ is etale by step 1. Base changing it over $A$ to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(b'')$, then restricting to the open $Y''_{b''}\subset U\times_A\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(b'')$, gives an etale $h_b:Y''_{b''}\to Y_b$, since $\kappa(b'')=\kappa(b)$, by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. It is flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism], hence open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. Its image is a nonempty open of the irreducible $Y_b$, so contains $\xi$. On the other hand every point of $Y''_{b''}$ is a specialization of $\xi''$, so its image is a specialization of $h_b(\xi'')$ by continuity. In particular $\xi$ is a specialization of $h_b(\xi'')$. The only point specializing to the generic point of an irreducible scheme is that generic point itself (the two points have the same closure and a scheme is $T_0$). Thus $h_b(\xi'')=\xi$.

source.place: Tag 05HR, generic-fibre basis after elementary etale refinement; openness is Tag 01UA (lemma-fppf-open).

proof.text:
For $\mathcal H=\pi_*\mathcal G$, the natural stalk formula [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback] and step 8 identify the residue-field map of $h^*\alpha$ at $\xi''$ with
$$\bigl(\alpha_\xi\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,\xi}}\kappa(\xi)\bigr)\otimes_{\kappa(\xi)}\kappa(\xi'').$$
Indeed associativity of tensor products identifies both its source and target with extension of scalars along the canonical field map $\kappa(\xi)\to\kappa(\xi'')$, since the local ring map sends the maximal ideal at $\xi$ into that at $\xi''$. Tensoring an isomorphism gives an isomorphism (tensor its inverse), so $\alpha''$ has the asserted generic residue-field property.

source.place: Tag 05HR, preservation of the map alpha on the generic residue-field vector space under the refinement.

proof.text: Finally $\mathcal H=\pi_*\mathcal G$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change](1), so $\mathcal Q=\operatorname{coker}\alpha$ is quasi-coherent and its sections on an affine open are the cokernel of the section map by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image]. For an affine open of $Y''$ over an affine open of $Y$, [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] computes pullback by tensoring the section modules, naturally in $\alpha$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], tensoring its cokernel sequence computes the cokernel of the tensored map. These natural identifications therefore give the canonical isomorphism $\operatorname{coker}\alpha''\cong h^*\mathcal Q$, with its quotient map. Together with the canonical pushforward comparison in step 7 and the field isomorphisms in steps 3--4, this proves all the remaining assertions.

source.place: Tag 05HR, pullback of Coker(alpha); Tag 02KG and tensor right exactness.

proof_origin.place: Tag 05HE (lemma-elementary-etale-neighbourhood), with the finite-pushforward and generic-basis comparisons used by Tag 05HR; auxiliary data omit support-dimension equalities.
